---
title: "Diagonal-Root Numerical Procedure"
subtitle: "How does root_hint initialize one reproducible loaded-root procedure?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design. The physical quantity remains
defined by the [Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#typed-direct-quantity-catalog);
this page fixes only its V1 numerical realization.

## Solve one scalar Schur residual

For the `exp(-i omega t)` convention, the complete loaded Direct operator is

$$
Q(\omega)=K-\omega^2C-i\omega G.
$$

The Primitive Direct V1 supports one retained coordinate $r$ and requires the
complete $C$ to be positive definite. This limitation avoids descriptor and
infinite-mode handling for `DiagonalRootSpec`; it does not restrict real-grid
Direct S/Y/Z.

The implementation first requires finite symmetric Float64 $C$ and evaluates
that condition with `cholesky(Symmetric(C); check=true)`. Factorization failure
is `UnsupportedSingularCapacitanceForDiagonalRootV1`; V1 adds no separate
eigenvalue cutoff or condition-number Gate.

With $E$ the eliminated complement, factorize $Q_{EE}$ and solve

$$
X=Q_{EE}^{-1}Q_{Er},\qquad
f=Q_{rr}-Q_{rE}X.
$$

For $Q'=-2\omega C-iG$, solve

$$
X'=Q_{EE}^{-1}(Q'_{Er}-Q'_{EE}X)
$$

and evaluate

$$
f'=Q'_{rr}-Q'_{rE}X-Q_{rE}X'.
$$

The baseline starts at real $\omega_0=2\pi\,\texttt{root_hint}$ and performs
at most 32 analytic complex-Newton updates

$$
\omega_{k+1}=\omega_k-\frac{f(\omega_k)}{f'(\omega_k)}.
$$

`root_hint` is only this deterministic initial locator. SCNSim does not sweep
for a minimum, enumerate the QEP spectrum, or replace the converged root with a
nearer eigenvalue.

## Require a machine-resolution certificate

Let $n$ be the complete operator dimension,
$\epsilon=\operatorname{eps}(\mathrm{Float64})$, and

$$
\tau(n)=256(n+1)\epsilon.
$$

Define $x_r=1$, $x_E=-X$ and

$$
A_{\rm abs}=|K|+|\omega||G|+|\omega|^2|C|.
$$

The Result is materialized only when all values are finite, $Q_{EE}$ is
solvable, $\operatorname{Re}\omega>0$, $\operatorname{Im}\omega\le0$, and
all four normalized errors are at most $\tau(n)$:

$$
\eta_E=
\frac{\|Q_{EE}X-Q_{Er}\|_\infty}
{\||Q_{EE}||X|+|Q_{Er}|\|_\infty},
\qquad
\eta_Q=
\frac{\|Q(\omega)x\|_\infty}
{\|A_{\rm abs}|x|\|_\infty},
$$

$$
\eta_f=\frac{|f|}{[A_{\rm abs}|x|]_r},
\qquad
\rho_\omega=\frac{|f/f'|}{|\omega|}.
$$

When $E$ is empty, its solve is a no-op and $\eta_E=0$. For a nonempty but
exactly decoupled complement, the $0/0$ eliminated-block ratio is likewise
defined as zero; a zero denominator with nonzero numerator is infinity and
fails the certificate. Other zero normalization denominators fail rather than
being replaced by an arbitrary floor.

With

$$
s_{f'}=|Q'_{rr}|+|Q'_{rE}||X|+|Q_{rE}||X'|,
$$

the normalized slope must also satisfy $|f'|/s_{f'}>\tau(n)$. The full
$Q(\omega)x$ residual is recomputed from C/G/K rather than reconstructed from
the Schur residual. Condition and slope evidence are recorded, but SCNSim adds
no separate design-quality threshold.

The normalized nonzero slope is machine-resolution evidence consistent with a
simple, locally isolated root. It is not a validated complex enclosure or a
proof of global uniqueness. V1 makes no claim that it found the root nearest to
`root_hint`; the hint selects the deterministic Newton basin only.

Bitwise stagnation means that the proposed update leaves both the real and
imaginary Float64 bit patterns of $\omega$ unchanged. It is success only if
this certificate passes. Otherwise the request returns
`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`,
`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`, or `RootSlopeUnresolved`. A missing, non-finite,
non-positive, or non-frequency `root_hint` returns `InvalidDiagonalRootHint`.
A non-positive-definite $C$ returns
`UnsupportedSingularCapacitanceForDiagonalRootV1`; it is not called
nonphysical.

## Continue every ParameterSet from the baseline

For a non-baseline ParameterSet, bind physical parameters in canonical SI and
follow

$$
p(t)=p_0+t(p_1-p_0),\qquad 0\le t\le1.
$$

Every candidate begins again at the sealed baseline root. Newton first attempts
the endpoint of the current interval. A numerical nonconvergence bisects that
interval and retries from its certified left endpoint, to a maximum depth of
32. After a midpoint succeeds, continuation resumes toward the original right
endpoint. It never uses the preceding CMA-ES candidate, reapplies `root_hint`,
or takes an automatic detour.

A repeated/unresolved slope, eliminated-block singularity, mapped physical
domain failure, or exhausted subdivision returns a typed non-continuable
failure. All constants, formulas, branching rules, and failure mappings are
part of the runtime algorithm ID.

This procedure fixes a reproducible baseline-owned numerical lineage, not a
validated enclosure of the entire analytic branch. A collision exposed by an
unresolved slope or failed continuation is rejected, but V1 does not claim to
detect every possible Newton-basin jump between certified endpoints. A global
branch proof would require a later enclosure-based algorithm and a new runtime
algorithm identity; complete-QEP nearest-root matching is not a substitute.
